meta.title: ON COMPUTE MARKETS
meta.subtitle: A simple manifesto for underwriting silicon risk

build_steps.title: Five steps from feed to cover

items.title: Pick a feed, not a vendor
items.text: Ingest public multi-provider GPU-hour prices — any source that returns normalized $/GPU-hour rows. No lock-in to one index publisher.

items.title: Score exposure on market facts
items.text: Map capacity at risk, tightness sensitivity, basis gap, and vol exposure from contracts plus live spot — seven sub-factors, fixed weights.

items.title: Score preparedness on instruments
items.text: Hedges, indices, parametric products, models, talent, capital — what exists to carry or transfer the bet.

items.title: Fuse, don't hallucinate
items.text: Blend register or index readings with research priors by evidence tier (λ). Arithmetic in code; agents supply inputs only.

items.title: Publish posture, price cover
items.text: Margin of Safety = Preparedness − Exposure. Parametric capacity and cost-band covers attach to the same indices the score uses.

items.title: Availability / tightness
items.text: Hours delivered vs contracted — the loss when the market tightens before price stabilizes.

items.title: Price volatility
items.text: Spot and forward repricing against fixed budgets — cost-band parametric on a published index.

items.title: Demand shocks
items.text: Open-weight release calendar — event overlay on availability and price limits.

items.title: Economic depreciation
items.text: Accounting life vs forward-implied residual — institutional only, forward curve required.

items.title: Grid coupling
items.text: Bridge to NFRI where compute sits on non-firm power — joint trigger, not a siloed GPU score.

blocks.text: Compute is priced like a commodity in the press and like a bespoke procurement exercise on the balance sheet. GPU-hour spot moves daily; multi-year contracts and damage-first BI do not. Nobody had published an outside-in map of who bears silicon-market risk versus who can underwrite it.

The Compute Market Underwriting Index (CMUI) scores buyers, clouds, brokers, carriers and reinsurers on the same plane: Exposure to compute-market loss (price, tightness, basis, shocks, depreciation, grid) versus Preparedness to carry or transfer it. One number — Margin of Safety = Preparedness − Exposure — plots posture, not pedigree.

This page is the construct in plain language: what we measure, how the arithmetic works, and how to build the pipeline from a live feed to a placeable parametric cover. The full spec lives in contract/COMPUTE_MODEL_SPEC.md; this is the manifesto.
Exposure asks how large the bet is. Preparedness asks whether the entity has the instruments to carry it. The scatter is a posture map — not a hazard league table.
Each axis is a weighted sum of sub-factors rated 0–4, rescaled to 0–100:
E = (Σ wi · reff,i / 4) × 100  ·  P likewise on preparedness  ·  MoS = P − E

Quadrants use in-sample medians on the current slice (exp ≥ {{fact:cut_exp}}, prep ≥ {{fact:cut_prep}}), not fixed 50/50. Negative MoS flags exposure running ahead of preparedness — the underwriting question the index is built around.

blocks.kicker: III · EXPOSURE — HOW LARGE IS THE BET

blocks.text: Seven sub-factors, weights sum to 1.00. Availability and price dominate; grid coupling is the NFRI bridge on linked UK assets.{{cite:ST-H100-VOLATILITY,ST-OPEN-WEIGHTS-RISK}}

blocks.caption: Exposure sub-factors — capacity, tightness, basis, vol, shocks, depreciation, grid.

blocks.kicker: IV · PREPAREDNESS — CAN THE FORM CARRY IT

blocks.text: Six sub-factors: hedge coverage, data and indices, product fit, pricing models, underwriting expertise, capital. MGAs score on product and telemetry; carriers on capital; buyers on hedges.{{cite:MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA,IND-GPU-INDICES}}

Every sub-factor carries a latent rating (research) and, where feeds or filings permit, a deterministic rating (index, contract, NFRI link). The published score is a credibility-weighted blend — never LLM output:{{cite:ACT-CREDIBILITY}}
reff = clamp(0,4, λ·rdet + (1−λ)·rlat) where λ rises with evidence tier: measured (0.95), derived (0.85), disclosed (0.80), assessed (0).

blocks.caption: Evidence tiers
rows: Live H100 median from public feed

blocks.kicker: VI · HOW TO BUILD THE MODEL

blocks.text: CMUI is designed to be rebuilt from public inputs. The harness does not depend on a single index vendor — any feed that returns normalized GPU-hour rows can drive the market layer.

blocks.caption: Pipeline — same shape as NFRI, different registers.

steps.title: Ingest feeds
steps.detail: Pull multi-provider spot (default: public REST). Snapshot to data/compute_indices/.

steps.title: Derive market
steps.detail: Median spot, cross-sectional spread as tightness proxy, rolling CV for vol exposure.

steps.title: Enrich entities
steps.detail: Update basis gap, tightness β, vol v on records with market_link. Propagate NFRI grid index.

steps.title: Fuse & score
steps.detail: compute_scoring.py — latent × deterministic blend, median-cut quadrants.

steps.title: Publish
steps.detail: compute_records.scored.json, dataset CSV, this page. Parametric triggers cite the same indices.

blocks.text: Products follow the peril stack: parametric capacity cover (hours delivered), cost band (index attachment), release overlay, then institutional depreciation and grid–compute bundles.{{cite:IND-COMPUTE-PARAMETRIC,CMUI-NFRI-BRIDGE}}

blocks.kicker: IX · THE INDEX AS PRICING OS

blocks.text: CMUI is not the cover — it is the operating system for placing it. Rate rises where MoS is negative and basis gap is wide; triggers must reference the same chip class and tenure as the insured's economic loss.{{cite:ACAD-BASIS-RISK-ARXIV,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}}

items: Capacity cover — pays on delivered GPU-hours below contract; index: tightness or SLA feed.
Cost band — pays when rolling index mean exceeds attachment.
Release overlay — reinstatement after named open-weight shock + joint index spike.
Grid–compute bundle — NFRI curtailment AND compute tightness joint trigger.
